data.narrative:
Gauss Fusion is a Series A-stage nuclear energy company that has raised €9M to date. The valuation analysis is anchored to a peer universe of 3 same-sector, same/adjacent-stage private companies (Valar Atomics at $6.0B Series B, Nano Nuclear Energy at $808M Seed, Fuse Energy at $200M Series A), supplemented by 8 additional private comparables and 3 public nuclear energy names (OKLO, NNE, SMR).

Two valuation methods are applicable. Stage-progression analysis uses the €9M raised as a proxy base and applies a 2.0x multiplier typical of Series A-to-next-stage progression, yielding $18M. Peer-median analysis calculates the median valuation across the 3-company filtered set at $808M, with a range of $200M (floor, Fuse Energy at Series A) to $6.0B (ceiling, Valar Atomics at Series B). The peer-median substantially exceeds the stage-progression result, reflecting material dispersion in early-stage nuclear funding outcomes.

Triangulating both methods produces a low-to-high range of $15M to $929M, with a median of $413M. The wide range reflects two material uncertainties: stage-progression yields a fundamentally different implied value than peer comparables, and the peer set itself spans three stages with a 30x spread. A credible valuation for Gauss Fusion would anchor toward the lower end absent evidence of differentiated technical or commercial progress versus Fuse Energy, while acknowledging upside to peer median if development trajectories align with Valar Atomics or Nano Nuclear Energy.
